title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing for partial JSON + delimiter/token ordering
author: Evan Chen
description: Summary: Fixes several edge cases in the SSE streaming layer that caused malformed partial-JSON payloads, incorrect delimiter insertion, and token/event ordering regressions when using the OpenAI-compatibility API surface. Motivation: Customers reported intermittent JSON parse errors and tool/function calling failures when responses are streamed and large payloads are chunked across multiple SSE events. This PR addresses three root causes: 1) incorrect buffer flush points in the chunking path that split JSON tokens across event boundaries, 2) a bug in the partial-JSON delimiter emitter that could emit the closing delimiter before emitting trailing token events, and 3) a race between the function-calling structured-output serializer and the SSE framing layer that led to token ordering inversion under load. Changes: - Rework chunk boundary detection to prefer semantic token boundaries using the tokenizer lookahead table; we now avoid flushes that split quoted strings or numeric tokens. - Introduce a deterministic delimiter emission policy: delimiters (partial-json start/end markers) are now queued and emitted only after all token events for the same logical frame have been enqueued. This prevents earlier closing delimiters being seen by clients before trailing tokens. - Add a lightweight per-request ordering fence in the streaming pipeline that guarantees in-order delivery of token events vs. delimiter/control events even when batching/aggregation kicks in. The fence is optimized to be a no-op in the common single-threaded path. - Update the OpenAI-compatibility adapter to preserve event ordering guarantees by propagating the ordering fence through the compatibility shim. This fixes cases where the adapter did additional buffering and reordered events. - Add unit and integration tests exercising chunking across quotes, escaped chars, long numbers, and nested structured outputs (function/tool call payloads). - Add a new e2e stress test that reproduces the original customer failure pattern with parallel streaming consumers and high-concurrency generation. Backwards compatibility and rollout: Changes are opt-in behind a feature flag sse_strict_ordering for a short canary period; we rolled it to Dedicated and Hosted Canary nodes for three days, observed zero parser errors in canary traffic, and then enabled it platform-wide. The feature is safe to disable for rollback (reverts to previous chunking heuristics). Testing & CI: Added new unit tests and synthetic integration harness; CI initially surfaced a flaky parser test that was fixed by increasing harness timeouts and stabilizing the ordering fence startup. All checks green on final run. Related: Linear ENG-2481 tracks the compatibility adapter follow-ups; SUP-1123 documents the customer support case. Checklist: - Repro case attached (yes) - Unit tests added (yes) - Integration stress test added (yes) - Docs note (streaming behavior) updated (yes) - Release notes drafted (yes).
